desk-look no longer paints a near-white bubble and band in a dark terminal when your Omarchy theme is light (or the reverse). When it can tell your terminal doesn't match the Omarchy theme, it leaves Claude Code's own look in place.

- The shaded surfaces (the repo/branch band above the input, your prompt bubbles, inline code and table headers, mode pills, pane backgrounds and diff colors) come from the host's Omarchy theme file. That file only describes the local terminal, so a dark remote terminal or a non-Omarchy terminal got light surfaces with unreadable text
- If Claude Code's `/theme` is set to `dark` or `light` (including the daltonized and ANSI variants) and it doesn't match the Omarchy theme, the surfaces are turned off, because Claude Code's own text colors would sink into them
- With `/theme` set to `auto` or a custom theme, the surfaces are turned off while a herdr remote client is attached, since that terminal's background is unknown. The remote check now also runs when herdr graphics are off, but only on session start and prompts as before, never on a timer
- Tip: if your terminal follows Omarchy and you want the surfaces locally, set `/theme` to `auto` or to the same brightness as your Omarchy theme
- desk-asana, desk-slack, desk-plan and desk-review move to 0.78.1 with no changes

## Install

```
/plugin install desk-look --marketplace KyongSik-Yoon/cc-desktop-mod
```

Already installed: `/desk-update` (or `claude plugin update desk-look`), then `/reload-plugins`.
